home.heroHeadingLine2: institutional memory will outlive any individual.
home.heroDescription: When experienced staff retire, when officers rotate, when federations merge — the precedents, relationships, and judgment they carry don’t transfer on their own. Union Eyes is the infrastructure that keeps it in place. Canadian-hosted. No worker surveillance. No black-box decisions.
home.outcomesDescription: Union Eyes is designed for leadership continuity, governance modernization, and democratic trust at scale.
home.xlateDescription: Union Eyes solves five operational problems that every long-running institution eventually faces — written in the language of the people doing the work, not the doctrine that explains why.
home.xlate1Title: It keeps decisions explainable when people change
home.xlate1Desc: When a president steps down, a treasurer rotates, or a key staffer leaves, the reasoning behind active grievances, financial commitments, and governance positions stays with the institution — not in someone’s head or inbox.
home.xlate2Title: It stops continuity loss during leadership transitions
home.xlate2Desc: New executives inherit a coherent operating picture instead of rebuilding context from scratch. Onboarding stops costing six months of institutional drift.
home.xlate3Title: It turns undocumented workflows into governed ones
home.xlate3Desc: The shadow processes that live in spreadsheets, side conversations, and personal practice become structured, reviewable, and inheritable — without surveilling the people who built them.
home.xlate4Title: It fits into how your institution already operates
home.xlate4Desc: Union Eyes is governance-shaped: it respects constitutional structures, executive mandates, and labour boundaries instead of forcing your institution to reshape itself around generic SaaS workflows.
home.xlate5Title: It is structurally different from workplace surveillance
home.xlate5Desc: No behavioural analytics. No productivity scoring. No member ranking. No cross-border data egress. Continuity infrastructure is not the same category as employee monitoring — and Union Eyes is built to prove it.
home.outcome1Desc: Leadership transitions retain strategic memory, governance context, and operational direction.
home.outcome2Desc: Every interpretation is bounded, evidence-anchored, and reviewer-of-record resolved.
home.outcome3Desc: Distributed teams work from one shared operating view instead of fragmented systems.

story.heroHeading: Two brothers. Two careers. One shared conviction.
story.heroDescription: A Labour Relations Officer turned lawyer and a seasoned technologist — together they are building the continuity substrate that unions have never had.
story.pageDescription: UnionEyes was founded by two brothers who lived the gaps in union infrastructure — and decided to close them.
story.originParagraph1: Michel spent years on the inside — first as a Labour Relations Officer for a national union, then as a lawyer conducting workplace investigations and assessments. Moving from working in a union to working with unions gave him an unfiltered view of where the friction lived: the workflows, the gaps, the moments where the right information simply wasn't in the right hands.
story.originParagraph2: Aubert took a different path. As a seasoned technologist, he made a career out of one idea — that technology should feel human. That the most powerful platforms are the ones people actually use.
story.originParagraph3: When their paths converged, the opportunity was obvious. Michel knew exactly what was broken. Aubert knew exactly how to fix it.
story.missionBody: Put the same clarity, accountability, and operational control that large organizations take for granted into the hands of every union — built by someone who lived it, and someone who knows how to scale it.
story.principle1Description: Technology serves people, never replaces them. Stewards make the decisions. The system provides support. There is no 'AI case manager.' There never will be.
story.principle2Description: We don't track 'organizer productivity' or 'case closure rates.' We don't build leaderboards. System health, yes. People surveillance, never.
story.principle3Description: Every grievance represents a person who was wronged. We treat that with the seriousness it deserves. No gamification. No corporate cheerfulness. Just respect.
story.principle4Description: UnionEyes has a reserved-matter governance structure. Union-elected representatives hold reserved oversight seats and exercise worker consent on change of control or mission change. This isn't marketing — it's in our shareholder agreement.
story.ctaHeading: Ready to see if we're the right fit?
story.ctaBody: We don't run generic demos. We run structured briefings tailored to your organization's continuity profile. Tell us about your challenges. We'll be honest about whether UnionEyes can help — or if something else would serve you better.
story.foundersIntro: UnionEyes was not assembled by a generalist software team that discovered the labour market. It was built by two named individuals with complementary, attestable domain experience.
story.founderMichelBio: Former Labour Relations Officer at a national union. Later, a lawyer conducting workplace investigations and assessments. Michel has worked inside unions, with unions, and across the procedural surface that UnionEyes is designed to support.
story.founderAubertBio: Career technologist focused on operational platforms that people actually use. Responsible for the architectural posture, deployment surface, and Canadian-hosted operational substrate of UnionEyes.
story.foundersNote: Both founders are reachable through the Executive Briefing channel — and remain operationally involved in every pilot deployment.

security.pageDescription: How UnionEyes protects your data with encryption, access controls, and continuous security monitoring.
security.heading: Security
security.intro: Union data is sensitive. We treat security as a foundational requirement, not an afterthought. This page outlines how UnionEyes protects your organization's information.
security.encryptionDesc: All data is encrypted in transit using TLS 1.2+ and at rest using AES-256. Database connections are encrypted end-to-end. Secrets and API keys are stored in Azure Key Vault — never in source code or environment files.
security.accessControlDesc: UnionEyes uses role-based access control (RBAC) to ensure members only see what they're authorized to see. Authentication is handled by Clerk with multi-factor authentication support. Database queries are scoped by organization to enforce strict data isolation between unions.
security.infrastructureDesc: UnionEyes is hosted on Microsoft Azure in Canadian data centres, ensuring your data stays within Canadian jurisdiction. We use container isolation, automated security scanning of dependencies and Docker images, and enforce strict Content Security Policy headers across all applications.
security.monitoringDesc: All access to sensitive data is logged with a full audit trail. We run automated vulnerability scanning on every code change, including static analysis (CodeQL), dependency audits, secret scanning, and container image scanning (Trivy). Rate limiting protects API endpoints from abuse.

trust.label: Trust posture
trust.posture: Trust in UnionEyes is operational, not symbolic. The surfaces below describe how explainability, governance review, sovereignty boundaries, and continuity-safe operation are enforced at runtime — not aspirations to be achieved later. Each pillar is reviewable by the institution's reviewer of record before any deployment commitment.

procurement.label: Procurement posture
procurement.posture: Programs are operational commitments, not subscriptions. Each maturity state names the institutional responsibilities UnionEyes will hold on the institution's behalf and the continuity-safe operating record it will maintain. Procurement reviewers are encouraged to read the maturity tiers as the institutional shape of the engagement — not as a feature ladder.

pilot.label: Pilot posture
pilot.posture: This is a continuity briefing, not a sales intake. The form below frames a bounded pilot whose success is measured in operational stabilization — fewer dropped commitments, clearer escalation, and an institutional record that survives leadership transitions. Workers are never the subject of pilot assessment.

ontology.label: Institutional ontology
ontology.posture: The eight surfaces below are not a feature list. They name the operational responsibilities a union, federation, or congress already carries. Adopting UnionEyes does not introduce new responsibilities — it gives the existing ones a continuity-safe operating record. Each pillar links to the runtime surface that fulfils it.

sovereignty.accessNote: Access is logged; actions taken here are part of the institutional record.

cognition.name: Cognition
cognition.posture: Bounded reasoning over institutional memory; outputs are recommendations for the reviewer of record, never operator-bypassing actions.

longitudinalCognition.name: Longitudinal cognition
longitudinalCognition.posture: Cross-time institutional reasoning; review continuity-relevant patterns before any escalation.

security.name: Security
security.posture: Continuity-critical configuration; changes are part of the institutional audit trail.

customerSuccess.name: Customer success
customerSuccess.posture: Institutional account stewardship; act on behalf of partner unions with reviewer-of-record discipline.

operations.name: Operations
operations.posture: Operational cadence and dispatch; sequence work as the reviewer of record for institutional execution.

ops.name: Sovereign ops
ops.posture: Sovereignty-layer runtime controls; every action is logged and continuity-affecting.

federation.heading: Governance-safe coordination across locals, councils, and federations.
